description: n26's input without `covered_through`. The event binds the prefix it extends and its own position, its attestation reaches none of the prefix (`attestedPrefixLength: 0`), and no coverage is claimed. An attestation that reaches nothing and claims nothing is a valid state; what n26 rejects is coverage claimed over it. This is the first of the two inputs on which @robertolocatelli81-dev's differential (#9) found his verifier and verify.py returning different verdicts; boundary_binding in MANIFEST.json now decides it. An engine that rejects an attested length of 0 whatever is claimed fails this vector. It is the accepting twin of n154, n156, n157, n158 and n170, each the same bytes with another value of `attestedPrefixLength`, and of n171, the same bytes with `covered_through: null` added.
